actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

dimensions.assessment: Applies across fifteen major federal agencies, departments, and the Environmental Protection Agency, affecting grant applicants and recipients nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: The head of a covered agency shall, with respect to each covered grant of the agency-- (1) include in any notice of funding opportunity... a clearly defined purpose

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new mandatory criteria for grant announcements, application prioritization, ongoing evaluations, and reporting to Congress.
dimensions.evidence: prioritize awarding the covered grant--(A) to applicants that have--(i) implemented practices that are evidence-based

dimensions.assessment: Affects the administration and allocation criteria of federal grant programs across major departments, though no specific spending authorization is added.
dimensions.evidence: The head of each covered agency shall submit an annual report to Congress on the activities carried out

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 5 of the United States Code to establish a broad government-wide grantmaking framework involving multiple executive departments and OMB guidance.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter II of chapter 3 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 315 the following: Sec. 316. Requirement to implement evidence-based practices

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory requirements and recurring annual reporting requirements for federal agencies and the OMB.
dimensions.evidence: Beginning on the date that is 5 years after the date of the enactment of this section, the head of each agency shall implement the framework

importance_detail.rationale: Requires major federal agencies and departments to implement evidence-based practices, evaluation standards, and community prioritization for certain public service grants.
